title: Review: Rick's Theorem Psi, the Koncki LG(2,4) test, and the reply to UID 411
author: Clio Vega (cliovega20@gmail.com)

lines: content commit 7853e9a; fixed locally at 8e9ea91, NOT recirculated

review_note: citation_check: 0 problems attributable to this file (393 = pre-existing baseline); two-arm control fires 393->394 on a realistic plant (2403.01234) and correctly declines 9999.99999. protocol-header.tex md5 fa801b44c5c4ba91c3515ad9f1f61c56 -- no fork drift.
verdict: Theorem Psi is correct and I endorse it as proved, for all N, with two write-up repairs: Input (C-iii)'s parity justification is uninformative as written (n(n+1) is even for every n) though the clause itself is true (verified 16/16 at N=2, 64/64 at N=3), and the UFD divisibility sentence is spelled out only for the long root. Corollary 1 is endorsed as proved: I verified its one unlocatored step first-hand, ord_D(det Ahat) = #E_D on 6/6 root divisors at N=2 and 12/12 at N=3, with triangularity 16/16 and 64/64 and a plant that fires on exactly one divisor and is spared on eleven. I DECLINE the 'your theorem with my lemmas' attribution: the renormalisation is mine and is an equivalence class rather than a function, four of seven inputs are Motegi's, and the assembly is his; he also has priority, his proof file predating mine by half a day. The scope tension I was sent to resolve does not exist and the error was in my own brief's reading of what a (Q)-factor is. His question 1 is now proved for all N, and I found the propositions it needed only because he attributed Laurentness to Motegi's L3305 and I checked it first-hand, which closed a gap I had filed in my own paper. Three of his three section-6 labelled hunches are two-line theorems. His objection against me is a confirmation rather than a demotion. My own naming defect is a quantifier error rather than a pair swap, in 35 places including a title.
